name: Copenhagen
tagline: Three Michelin stars of Nordic cuisine, and the smørrebrød that's been served the same way since 1877.

Geranium.description: Avant-garde Nordic cuisine named the world's best restaurant in 2022 and 2023. Three Michelin stars, reviewed by critic Andy Hayler.

Restaurant Schønnemann.description: A smørrebrød institution since 1877, with more than 100 hand-written variations on the menu.

Kadeau.description: A piece of Bornholm island in Christianshavn, with seasonal Danish ingredients. Three Michelin stars.

Jordnær.description: Just 25 seats on the first floor of the Gentofte Hotel, run by the Vildgaard couple. Three Michelin stars.

Noma.description: René Redzepi's lab on Refshalevej, the birthplace of modern Nordic cuisine. The sole focus of the Copenhagen episode of "Parts Unknown."

Alchemist.description: A roughly seven-hour tasting journey of about 50 'impressions' blending avant-garde cooking, art and theatre in a former industrial space on Refshaleøen. Two Michelin stars and a regular in the top 10 of The World's 50 Best Restaurants.

AOC.description: Nordic cuisine with French roots served in the vaulted cellars of the historic Moltkes Palæ, near Kongens Nytorv. Two Michelin stars.

Marchal.description: Hotel d'Angleterre's restaurant, blending French technique with Nordic ingredients, overlooking Kongens Nytorv. One Michelin star since 2014.

Barr.description: Set in Noma's original Strandgade address, Thorsten Schmidt serves rustic North Sea dishes rooted in classic Nordic tradition. Listed in the Michelin Guide.

Alouette.description: A tiny restaurant tucked into a former workshop in Islands Brygge, run by American chef Nick Curtin. One Michelin star since 2019.

Höst.description: A candlelit, cozy Nordic bistro from the Cofoco restaurant group. Holds a Bib Gourmand for exceptional value.

Silberbauers Bistro.description: A Niçoise-leaning bistro with seasonal seafood, opened in 2021 in Jægersborggade's former Manfreds space by an ex-Relæ chef. Bib Gourmand.

Bæst.description: A pizzeria from Christian Puglisi's group (ex-Noma) with house-made mozzarella and charcuterie, in the heart of Nørrebro.

Mirabelle.description: Puglisi's former bakery turned Sicilian-style trattoria and natural wine bar, in the same building as Bæst.

Sanchez.description: Contemporary Mexican cooking from Rosio Sanchez, Noma's former head pastry chef, in Vesterbro.

Hija de Sanchez.description: Rosio Sanchez's taco stand inside Torvehallerne, making tortillas by hand from corn imported from Mexico. Named best street food in Europe by EasyJet Traveller magazine in 2018.

Aamanns 1921.description: A modern take on traditional smørrebrød by Adam Aamann, using house-baked bread and house-cured ingredients.

Restaurant Kronborg.description: Smørrebrød served in a 17th-century building on the corner of Brolæggerstræde and Knabrostræde, cannonball still lodged in the facade. Berlingske food critic Søren Frank has praised its no-frills execution of the classics.

Slotskælderen hos Gitte Kik.description: A smørrebrød restaurant since 1910 near Christiansborg, with the whole menu laid out on a long table. Traditionally a haunt of Danish politicians.

Torvehallerne.description: A covered market of two glass-and-steel pavilions on Israels Plads, opened in 2011 on the site of the old Grønttorv wholesale market. Home to dozens of producer stalls and market kitchens.

La Banchina.description: A waterfront natural wine bar and cafe on Refshaleøen, with a sauna and an official harbour swimming spot.

Absalon.description: A former church turned community house in Vesterbro, where over 100 strangers share a three-course vegetarian dinner every night.

Coffee Collective.description: A pioneering specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Scandinavia, founded in 2007 by world-championship-winning baristas, with its original shop on Jægersborggade.

Democratic Coffee.description: A specialty coffee bar next to the Copenhagen Main Library, known for its almond croissants baked fresh on site and light-roast single-origin coffee.

Meyers Bageri.description: An organic bakery from the group of Claus Meyer, co-founder of New Nordic Cuisine, with a shop on Jægersborggade.

Lagkagehuset.description: A Danish bakery chain born in 1991 on Torvegade, famous for its spandauer pastries and fresh-baked bread.

John's Hotdog Deli.description: A hot dog cart near Central Station run by John Michael Jensen, using Bornholm sausages and homemade remoulade. Anthony Bourdain tried his wild-garlic-and-bacon 'deluxe' dog on 'Parts Unknown.'

DØP.description: A 100% organic hot dog stand by the Round Tower, serving organic sausages on wholegrain buns. Named Copenhagen's best fast-food spot in 2010, ahead of Michelin-starred restaurants.

Grøften.description: Tivoli Gardens' oldest restaurant, open since 1874, known for its frikadeller and checkered-tablecloth charm.

Nimb Brasserie.description: A French-style brasserie inside the Moorish palace of Hotel Nimb, in Tivoli Gardens.

Kødbyens Fiskebar.description: A seafood restaurant set in a former butcher's shop in the Meatpacking District, serving oysters and sustainably sourced Nordic fish.

Cofoco.description: The founding restaurant of the Copenhagen Food Consulting group, opened in 2004, serving affordably priced, internationally inspired Nordic food in Vesterbro.

Llama.description: A South American restaurant from the Cofoco group specializing in ceviche, anticuchos and Uruguayan-style grilled meats, in central Copenhagen.

La Glace.description: Copenhagen's oldest patisserie, open since 1870, famous for its 'Sportskage' of meringue, cream and hazelnut.

Sankt Peders Bageri.description: Copenhagen's oldest bakery, operating since 1652, known for its giant Wednesday-only cinnamon buns, 'onsdagssnegle.'

Reffen.description: Northern Europe's largest street food market, with around 35 stalls and its own brewery, on the Refshaleøen peninsula.

Mikkeller Bar.description: The original bar of Danish craft brewery Mikkeller, opened in 2012 in Vesterbro, with around twenty rotating taps.

Ved Stranden 10.description: A natural and biodynamic wine bar by the canal, long regarded as one of Copenhagen's best wine bars.

Lidkoeb.description: A cocktail bar in the courtyard of a former 1886 pharmacy on Vesterbrogade, sister bar to Ruby. A regular on The World's 50 Best Bars list.

Ruby.description: A cocktail bar in a 1740 townhouse by the Nybrogade canals, ranked among the world's 50 best bars by The World's 50 Best Bars.
